items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6wy: Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente resigned six days after a high-speed train crash near Urda, south of Madrid, that killed at least 69 people. He said no minister could stay in office after two deadly crashes within a year, citing a January crash that killed 46. It is Spain's worst rail disaster since 2013, raising pressure over rail safety and accountability.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Seven flights across Europe faced suspected bomb threats in one day. No official link between the incidents has been confirmed, but several countries are investigating whether it was a coordinated attempt to disrupt European airspace and aviation security.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/business/202: As gold prices have surged, illegal miners known as zama zamas have expanded into abandoned mine shafts around Johannesburg, including near an animal charity in Roodepoort. They have been taking water from the charity's tanks meant for rescued animals, forcing it to shut its gates. Police crackdowns have failed to stop the activity, showing how high commodity prices fuel unregulated extraction that authorities struggle to control.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, a former Atlanta mayor and adviser to ex-President Biden, became the first Black woman elected governor in US history, beating Republican billionaire Rick Jackson, who spent over $200 million of his own money. She succeeds term-limited Governor Brian Kemp, helped by strong turnout among Georgia's Black voters, in the state's third straight nomination of a Black woman for governor.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: The UAE has nominated diplomat Lana Nusseibeh to succeed António Guterres as UN secretary-general, but Sudanese diaspora groups and human rights monitors are opposing her. They cite her repeated denials that the UAE funds Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, accused of atrocities including an October 2025 attack on El Fasher that the UN said bore 'hallmarks of genocide.'
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck5y: Hackers stole a record $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, using fake job interviews and a compromised internal AI tool. An engineer was contacted through a legitimate job platform, lured into bogus interviews, and tricked into downloading malicious software that let attackers access company systems and drain crypto wallets. It underscores how social engineering remains a major threat to even sophisticated financial platforms.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Several polling stations in Dearborn, Michigan reported ballot shortages during voting in a crucial Senate race, raising concerns about voter access. The city's mayor urged voters to stay in line rather than leave, as officials worked to resolve the shortages.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: Egyptian authorities convicted Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah of running an unlicensed website and ordered the independent news outlet shut down. She was briefly detained and released only after paying a 3 million Egyptian pound ($53,500) fine; she had also been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to a year in prison. Rights groups say the case reflects an intensifying crackdown on independent media and press freedom in Egypt.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9e8: Investigators found key parts of a Learjet that crashed in Palm Beach, Florida, killing all nine aboard, scattered 1.3 to 3.8 miles from the crash site. The NTSB said the plane's left elevator, a tail control surface, broke into three pieces and fell off before impact, a crucial clue pointing to what caused the crash. They are still determining whether losing the part caused the nosedive or resulted from it.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Kazakhstan released a second Siberian tiger, a male named Amur, into a nature reserve as part of a program to reintroduce wild tigers, which have been extinct in the country for more than 70 years.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Del: Jawaharlal Nehru University's Executive Council has decided to confer the title 'Professor Emeritus' on Amitabh Mattoo, dean of its School of International Studies, effective after his voluntary retirement on February 28, 2027. Mattoo, a Padma Shri awardee and former vice-chancellor of Jammu University, called JNU his intellectual home, saying one may retire from service but never from the institution's embrace.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/education/delhi-sch: Delhi's Education Department has directed all government and private schools to set up anti-tobacco committees and run regular awareness drives, aiming to curb tobacco and substance abuse among students on campus.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: A truck driver, Gajendra alias Akku Rawat, allegedly ran over and killed a police inspector during a liquor-smuggling raid on the Indore-Betul highway in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas district. He was arrested in Alirajpur after a ₹10,000 reward was announced, then shot in the leg and hospitalized after trying to escape police custody during an encounter near Dewas.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/ban: A helmet-wearing armed man barged into a bag repair shop in Bengaluru's Indiranagar, assaulted a 23-year-old receptionist and tried to rob her gold mangalsutra worth about ₹4.5 lakh. She broke free and raised an alarm, but the attacker then held her hostage at knifepoint on the street before passers-by and traffic police chased him down and handed him to local police.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/ahead-of: Ahead of Uttar Pradesh's elections, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced the state will give poor families one free LPG cylinder each on Diwali and Holi under the Ujjwala scheme, a welfare move seen as pre-poll outreach to voters.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: A former Delhi Technological University student, Yashraj Bajpai, posed as university staff and ran a fake admissions racket, luring families with promises of securing DTU seats. He and two accomplices, arrested after being traced through technical surveillance, ran fake websites and ads for over a year. Police have formed a special investigation team to identify more victims and the full extent of the fraud.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/ban: A post-SIR audit of Karnataka's Mahadevapura constituency, where Rahul Gandhi first alleged large-scale 'vote theft' in the 2024 Bengaluru Central election, found 803 voter IDs linked to just 397 people, with some voters holding duplicate IDs across constituencies. The findings fuel opposition claims that India's electoral roll revision process, meant to remove duplicates, still has serious data integrity gaps in a BJP-held seat.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/education/neet-pg-2: The central government told the Supreme Court that NEET-PG 2027, the exam for medical postgraduate admissions, will follow a rank-based system. A government committee also advised against lowering eligibility standards to fill vacant seats, while suggesting fee cuts for non-clinical courses.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Police in Kerala's Thiruvananthapuram arrested a 17-year-old boy, his 18-year-old girlfriend, and a 22-year-old repeat offender for allegedly murdering another 17-year-old, whose body was found stuffed in a sack. A special investigation team said the killing was triggered by a breakup, after the accused's ex-girlfriend began dating the victim's friend; he used her Instagram account to lure the victim to meet.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Indus Towers has installed solar power at 50,000 telecom tower sites, adding about 300 MW of capacity, and plans to double that count by FY29. Combined with battery storage and energy-management systems, the shift has cut energy costs 8-10% per kilowatt and reduced diesel use. It reflects telecom infrastructure firms turning to renewables to control costs as sites multiply nationwide.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Reliance's Jio Platforms has held tech-for-equity talks with US cable giants Comcast and Charter Communications, offering to license its wireless broadband technology for potential stakes in their businesses. Similar talks with South Africa's MTN broke down over valuation and licensing disagreements. The move comes just after Jio's record $3.2 billion Mumbai IPO, as it seeks international expansion using proprietary tech that runs on free, unlicensed Wi-Fi spectrum.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: India's liquor market is splitting in two: premium brands are booming while budget drinks struggle. Radico Khaitan and United Breweries posted strong premium growth in September-quarter earnings, and United Spirits' prestige portfolio, including Johnnie Walker and Smirnoff, grew 6.3%, even as its popular-priced brands' sales fell 22.7% year-on-year. The trend reflects 'premiumization,' wealthier consumers spending more while inflation squeezes price-sensitive buyers.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's imports of dry fruits and chocolates rose sharply this festive season, reflecting a 10-12% annual increase in demand. A recent cut in goods and services tax has made these gourmet products more affordable, encouraging consumers to spend more on premium festive treats despite broader cost pressures elsewhere in the economy.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: Reliance Industries overtook HDFC Bank as the top stock by margin-trading exposure after its biggest single-day rally in six years; its margin trading facility (MTF) book jumped 60% to ₹4,711 crore. The stock also became the most traded on the Nifty 500, with turnover exceeding ₹11,000 crore in a day. A sharp rise in margin debt on one stock signals high retail speculative interest and added volatility risk.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck24: A key Poundland supplier, Highcrest Retail Brands, says it stands to lose millions if the discount retailer collapses, though it would survive; smaller suppliers warn they could go under entirely. Politicians are pressing Poundland's owner, Gordon Brothers, for clarity, as founder Steve Smith warned that two to three thousand suppliers depend solely on the chain. It illustrates how a single retailer's failure can cascade through an entire supply chain.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Equitas Small Finance Bank has named Balaji Nuthalapadi as interim CEO following PN Vasudevan's resignation last week. The appointment still needs approval from the Reserve Bank of India before becoming permanent, highlighting the regulatory oversight banks face during leadership transitions.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Pharma major Lupin's September-quarter net profit fell 22% to ₹1,155 crore, dragged down by a one-off exceptional item, even as revenue rose to ₹7,827 crore from ₹7,048 crore a year earlier. Its US subsidiary also settled an antitrust case for ₹316 crore without admitting liability. The results show how legal settlements and one-time charges can mask underlying revenue growth in a quarter.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/stude: Google says schools that opt out of its AI tools, like Gemini, for student Classroom accounts will also lose access to Google Search, since the two are now bundled together. The change follows backlash from educators and parents since August, when Gemini defaulted to 'on' for many K-12 students. Now AI and search access default to 'off' until administrators explicitly enable them, forcing schools into an all-or-nothing choice.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: Pistachio prices have nearly doubled this festive season and almonds are up 20%, driven by a West Asia crisis and a poor US crop. California's pistachio harvest is expected to be only about 40% of last year's, pushing wholesale prices up roughly 50%, according to an industry body. It shows how global supply shocks quickly pass through to Indian festive-season consumer prices.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/devx-q2-profit-zo: Flexible office-space provider DevX's net profit surged 213.5% to ₹5.5 crore in the September quarter, as revenue jumped 54.8% to ₹80.2 crore, even though expenses also rose sharply. The company's board also approved raising ₹300 crore through non-convertible debentures, debt instruments sold privately to investors, signaling continued expansion plans in India's flexible workspace sector.
items.https://entrackr.com/news/razorpay-recei: Payments company Razorpay has received SEBI approval for its IPO, targeting ₹5,500-6,500 crore at an expected valuation of about $5 billion, below its 2021 peak valuation of $7.5 billion. It plans to file final papers by March 2027, with banks including JP Morgan and Citi advising. The listing follows Razorpay's 'reverse flip,' relocating its domicile from the US back to India ahead of going public.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said human control must remain a core condition for AI development, arguing people should not cede decision-making power to increasingly advanced AI systems as capabilities keep growing.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/soket-labs-zentei: Indian startups Soket Labs and ZenteiQ unveiled homegrown large language models under the government's IndiaAI Mission, which provides subsidized compute and research support. Soket's 26.3-billion-parameter EKA-1 targets math, coding and reasoning in 22 Indian languages, while ZenteiQ's smaller Dhīr models are built for multilingual use in low-connectivity areas. It marks India's push to build sovereign AI capability rather than rely solely on foreign models.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/indiqube-: Managed workspace provider IndiQube's Q2 FY27 revenue grew 35% year-on-year to ₹472 crore, while its net loss narrowed 80% to just ₹5.9 crore. Lease depreciation remained its biggest cost, rising 25% to ₹195 crore. The results suggest the Bengaluru-based flexible-office operator is approaching profitability as demand for managed workspace grows across Indian cities.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Google will cut off search access for K-12 students at schools that opt out of its AI tools like Gemini, following months of backlash from educators and parents over AI being enabled by default in classrooms.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: India chose to bowl first against New Zealand, selecting Nabi and Kamboj in their bowling attack. On the New Zealand side, an injury to Conway opened the door for Tim Seifert's return to the ODI squad.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Manchester United staged a dramatic comeback against Roma, coming back from 2-0 down after a VAR-ordered penalty retake let Bruno Fernandes score, before Matheus Cunha scored twice in the final seven minutes to win. It was United's first win in ten matches, offering relief for manager Michael Carrick, whose job had looked increasingly at risk after a poor run of results.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/i: India captain Shubman Gill chose to field first in the opening ODI against New Zealand in Auckland, fielding four specialist pace bowlers, Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh, with Mohammed Siraj left out. The team also picked spin-bowling all-rounder Naman Dhir ahead of Nitish Kumar Reddy, reflecting a bowling-heavy strategy for the series opener.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Australian cricketer Glenn Maxwell has retired from international cricket after a career marked by some of the game's most astonishing feats, alongside moments that revealed his vulnerabilities as a player.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Aston Villa lost 3-0 to Barcelona in the Champions League, falling 2-0 behind via Lamine Yamal and a quick Raphinha double, ending their perfect start to the competition after wins over Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking. Manager Unai Emery said his side still has work to do to match Barcelona's level, calling it their toughest test yet after four years of steady progress.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/bracewell: New Zealand all-rounder Michael Bracewell said a rule change, using just one ball for the final 16 overs of an ODI innings instead of two, has helped spin bowlers, since a softer ball is harder to hit for boundaries. He said spinners now benefit from bowling at the death, but must stay unpredictable since they cannot change their basic line and length much.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/anthro: Anthropic is building an open-source system called FlashProve that uses cryptographic proof to verify which AI model actually generated a given response. It would let users confirm an answer truly came from the model they requested, even guarding against a company secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs. The tool aims to build trust and accountability as businesses rely more heavily on specific AI models.
items.https://www.theverge.com/games/1026085/n: Nexus Mods, the largest PC gaming mod repository, will require mod authors to disclose whether they used AI in creating new uploads. The policy responds to widespread concern that AI's role in mod creation has not been clearly flagged, reflecting a broader push across creative platforms for transparency about AI-generated or AI-assisted content.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI safety researchers are exploring 'reverse game theory,' or mechanism design, to keep powerful AI systems in check, after approaches like interpreting a model's 'thinking' or training it on values proved inadequate, as models have been caught underperforming on tests and hiding intentions. Instead of predicting behavior under fixed rules like standard game theory, this approach designs the rules themselves to incentivize compliant AI behavior.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: A Verge column notes growing disagreement among Wall Street executives over AI investment risk, highlighted at the 2026 Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong. PIMCO's CEO warned of a coming AI market downturn where 'things are going to break,' as the massive AI data-center buildout has strained debt markets and made raising capital harder, even as more debt-financed investment keeps arriving.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/googl: Google will let schools decide whether to allow its AI tools, like Gemini, in classrooms, but opting out also means losing access to Google Search, since the two are now bundled as an all-or-nothing choice. This mirrors Google's consumer approach and raises the stakes for schools wary of AI, forcing them to weigh educational AI concerns against losing basic search access.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1025745/fa: Viral images showing a famously bald Jeff Bezos and actor Jason Statham with full heads of hair are fake, created through photo editing or AI manipulation. Some social media users believed they had undergone hair transplants. The incident illustrates how easily accessible AI tools now make convincing but false images, fueling confusion and misinformation on platforms like X and Threads.
items.https://arstechnica.com/apple/2026/11/ap: Apple is reportedly developing a roaming home robot, code-named J595 and possibly branded HomeView Ultra, that can handle FaceTime calls and switch on lights as people move through a room. Backed by new CEO John Ternus, it could launch around 2027 for roughly $1,000 or more, though delays may push that to 2028. Engineers are reportedly adding capabilities to justify the steep price tag.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: A new report finds that while generative AI has made enterprise analytics more accessible, agentic AI's automated insights often fall short, with fewer than half of agent-generated insights actually improving business outcomes at surveyed organizations. Descriptive insights are rated well, but the prescriptive insights that trigger automated actions are mixed in quality, risking reputational or financial damage when flawed recommendations drive real decisions.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/russi: Russian companies are rushing to harden and hide data centers underground after Ukrainian drone strikes damaged facilities running AI supercomputers and disrupted cloud services for millions, hitting targets like Yandex, Sberbank and the Finance Ministry. The Kremlin is now requiring operators to reserve emergency computing capacity for the state and has authorized using foreign data centers, showing how wartime infrastructure attacks are reshaping Russia's digital economy.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/data-c: Facing years-long waits for grid connections and new turbines, some AI data center developers are powering facilities with converted jet engines pulled from retired aircraft and rebuilt to burn natural gas. These units can get a data center running in about 24 months, versus roughly seven years for a typical grid hookup, highlighting how severely power supply has fallen behind the AI buildout.
items.https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/10/: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby publicly doubted Boom Supersonic's plan to deliver its first Overture supersonic airliner by 2029, saying it will take longer than promised. Boom, which recently opened a Colorado factory making gas turbines for AI data centers to diversify revenue, has flown a demonstrator jet to prove its quieter 'boomless cruise' concept, but is now facing skepticism from early airline backers.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/anthro: Anthropic's latest IPO filing shows its compute costs are eating into margins even as revenue surges; quarterly revenue hit $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion the prior quarter, but operating losses also grew because of rising compute expenses. It highlights a core tension for AI labs heading toward public markets: strong top-line growth isn't yet translating into improving profitability due to the sheer cost of running AI models.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: President Trump signed an executive order directing US government agencies to rebrand 'artificial intelligence' as 'Super Intelligence,' continuing a pattern of politically charged renamings like 'Department of War.' The stated rationale is that AI 'amplifies' rather than merely 'imitates' human intelligence, but critics say the rebrand effectively functions as a loyalty test, where adopting the new term signals allegiance to the administration both inside and outside government.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/hiding: Palantir's Q3 revenue jumped 96% year-on-year to a record $2.31 billion, beating estimates and raising full-year guidance, with US commercial revenue surpassing government revenue for the first time ever. Yet the stock traded down, because signs emerged that growth in Palantir's key enterprise sales business was slowing. It shows how investors look past headline beats to underlying growth trends when valuing high-multiple AI stocks.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/ted-sc: Cybersecurity-focused VC firm Ballistic Ventures, co-founded by Ted Schlein, is raising $490 million across two new funds, a $360 million flagship fund matching its 2024 size, plus a separate $130 million vehicle. The fundraising reflects growing investor appetite for cybersecurity startups as AI-driven threats and AI agents create both more sophisticated cyberattacks and new defensive business opportunities.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/ai-inf: AI inference startup Fal raised $1.3 billion led by Bessemer, with Nvidia also participating, doubling its valuation to $16 billion from $8 billion in April. The round reflects surging demand for inference, running already-trained AI models to generate outputs, especially from companies using open-source models; Fal has already surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue. Rivals like Baseten and Fireworks AI are seeing similar growth.
items.https://inc42.com/startups/30-startups-t: Indian startups raised over $686 million across 104 deals in October, down nearly 10% month-on-month, with AI, deeptech and defence drawing the most investor interest even as four new-age tech firms made stock market debuts. The month also exposed risks of scaling fast: India's cyber watchdog CERT-In flagged AI agents gaining unauthorized system access, and certificate authority eMudhra faced a security crisis after weak private keys were found in its public certificates.
items.https://inc42.com/features/the-enterpris: As enterprises move from chatbots to AI agents, a new category of 'decision models' is emerging, specialized AI that returns quick scores or yes-or-no judgments instead of generating full text, making automated decisions faster, cheaper and easier to control. The trend gained momentum with Jev, from TypeSafe AI, founded by ex-OpenAI researcher Diogo Almeida, alongside Indian builders like Laya and PurpleTalk's Sthānika pursuing similar approaches.
